I added `addNote(String orderId, String note)` to `OrderFacade` and a nullable `note()` component to `OrderSummary`. The full test suite passes, including the ArchUnit architecture rules.

- **`OrderFacade` / `OrderSummary`** (`orders/api`): new `addNote` method, and `OrderSummary` now takes `note` as its last component.
- **`Order`** (`orders/internal`): holds a `note` field, `null` until set, with a getter and a `changeNote` setter.
- **`OrderService`** (`orders/internal`): `addNote` is `@Transactional` and sets the note; `summary` maps it into the record.

A second `addNote` call replaces the existing note rather than appending to it, since the spec called for a single `note()` value. Calling it with an unknown order ID throws `NoSuchElementException`, as the other order methods do. I didn't add a dedicated test for the new behaviour.

# 7. API types do not expose internals

Date: 2026-07-20

## Status

Accepted

## Context

Returning an entity from a facade lets every caller depend on its shape, so renaming a field in `internal` breaks other modules.

## Decision

Nothing in an `api` package refers to a type in an `internal` package. A facade returns a record declared in its own `api` package.

## Consequences

There is a small mapping step between entities and API records.

`PaymentsFacade.paymentsOf` predates this decision and is scheduled for migration. It is not a pattern to follow.

# 1. Record architecture decisions

Date: 2026-03-02

## Status

Accepted

## Context

We keep having the same design discussions, because nobody can find out why the code looks the way it does.

## Decision

We record each decision that is expensive to reverse as a short, numbered file in `docs/adr`. An accepted record is not edited: a new record supersedes it.

## Consequences

Decisions, including the options we rejected, can be read in the repository, and reviewed like code.
